summary: Configured PostgreSQL 15 streaming replication across the RHEL 7.9 cluster: node1 is the writable primary, node2 and node3 are read-only streaming standbys. Verified data replicates from primary to both standbys, standbys reject writes, and the setup survives a sequential restart of all three nodes (standbys first, primary last) with full replication and data recovery confirmed afterward.
actions_performed: Surveyed all three nodes: RHEL 7.9, no PostgreSQL installed, RHEL base repo (rhel-7-server-rpms) available but PGDG EL7 repos for PG 12-14 returned 410 Gone

Installed PGDG repo RPM on node1/node2/node3, resolved missing libicu/libzstd deps by adding an EPEL 7 archive repo (dl.fedoraproject.org/pub/archive/epel/7), installed postgresql15-server + postgresql15 on all three nodes

Ran initdb on node1 (primary), configured postgresql.conf (wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders, max_replication_slots, hot_standby=on) and pg_hba.conf (scram-sha-256 host entries for replication and normal connections from the cluster subnet)
Opened firewalld port 5432/tcp on all three nodes; started/enabled postgresql-15 on node1

Generated a replication password with openssl on node1, created the `replicator` REPLICATION LOGIN role, transferred the password file directly node1->node2/node3 over cluster SSH keys (never printed the secret in tool output), then shredded the temp files afterward
Wiped node2/node3 data directories and ran pg_basebackup -R from node1 to build both standbys with standby.signal and primary_conninfo auto-configured
Started/enabled postgresql-15 on node2 and node3, verified pg_stat_replication showed both streaming and pg_is_in_recovery()=true on both standbys
Created repl_test table and inserted rows on the primary; confirmed identical data on both standbys and confirmed standbys reject INSERTs (read-only)
Captured pre-restart boot_id baseline plus PostgreSQL/replication health on all three nodes
Sequentially rebooted node2, then node3, then node1 (primary) via systemctl reboot backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect; polled each node until SSH/exec was available again

Confirmed changed boot_id on every node post-restart, confirmed postgresql-15 active and pg_is_in_recovery() correct on each node after its restart, confirmed pg_stat_replication showed both standbys streaming again after the primary's restart
Performed a final post-restart write on the primary and confirmed it replicated to both standbys immediately

evidence.requirement: node1 configured as writable primary with wal_level/replication settings and replication role
evidence.summary: initdb run, postgresql.conf/pg_hba.conf updated for replication, postgresql-15 started, replicator role created

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 configured as read-only standbys via pg_basebackup streaming replication
evidence.summary: pg_basebackup -R completed on both nodes creating standby.signal and primary_conninfo pointing at node1; postgresql-15 started and active

evidence.requirement: Primary sees both standbys streaming; standbys report pg_is_in_recovery=true
evidence.summary: pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both 10.100.135.11 and 10.100.135.12 in state 'streaming'; both standbys return pg_is_in_recovery()=t

evidence.requirement: Changes committed on primary are visible on both standbys
evidence.summary: Table created and rows inserted on node1; identical rows immediately visible via SELECT on node2 and node3
INSERT on node2 fails with 'cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction'

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 9294b73f...; systemctl reboot acked and connection dropped; boot_id changed to ea957b29... on reconnect; postgresql-15 active, pg_is_in_recovery=t, repl_test count=2; primary shows node2 streaming again

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 33b0e84c...; reboot acked and connection dropped; boot_id changed to 2242e162... on reconnect; postgresql-15 active, pg_is_in_recovery=t, repl_test count=2; primary shows node3 streaming again

evidence.requirement: node1 (primary) restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state including replication resumption
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 0571f4dd...; reboot acked and connection dropped; boot_id changed to 863950ba... on reconnect; postgresql-15 active, pg_is_in_recovery=f (primary), data intact; both standbys reconnected and streaming again (node2 log shows walreceiver reconnect and resumed streaming; node3 pg_is_in_recovery=t)
New row inserted on primary after all three restarts; identical row immediately visible on both node2 and node3
